items.dek: Drake Maye put up 26.8 PPR points. How it happened, every fantasy-relevant line, who's rising, who's falling and who to grab off waivers.
body: The Bears pulled away from the Patriots for a 30-24 win. The Bears are now 5-2, and the Patriots slip to 4-3.

The Bears got on the board first, in the first quarter, on a 43-yard field goal by Cairo Santos. The offenses traded blows all day: six touchdowns in all, which is exactly what fantasy managers want to see.

Caleb Williams delivered: he finished 22 of 33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns. That's 22.2 PPR points, 3.4 better than our 18.8 projection. D'Andre Swift paid off for his managers: he carried 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown, adding four catches for 12 yards. That's 19.0 PPR points, 3.2 better than our 15.8 projection. He handled 92% of the running back carries, and that kind of volume travels week to week. Colston Loveland stole the show: he caught seven of 12 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown. Good for 19.9 PPR points against an 11.3 projection; a new season high. With 40% of the team's targets, he is clearly the first read. Luther Burden III was the story: he caught all four of his targets for 130 yards and a touchdown. Good for 23.7 PPR points against an 11.9 projection; a new season high. Rome Odunze did his job: he caught four of five targets for 69 yards. That's 10.9 PPR points, right around the 9.8 we expected.

Drake Maye delivered: he finished 23 of 28 for 305 yards and two touchdowns, with an interception, plus 26 yards on the ground and a rushing score. That's 26.8 PPR points, 7.1 better than our 19.7 projection. Rhamondre Stevenson broke out: he carried six times for 22 yards, adding five catches for 93 yards and a receiving score. Good for 22.5 PPR points against a 12.2 projection, his best game of the season. Don't read too much into it yet; he split the work, taking 46% of the running back carries. Hunter Henry delivered: he caught all seven of his targets for 71 yards. That's 14.1 PPR points, 5.5 better than our 8.6 projection. Eli Raridon stole the show: he caught three of four targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. That's 14.6 PPR points, more than double the 5.7 we projected, easily his top game of the year. A.J. Brown never got going: he caught three of five targets for 48 yards. Just 7.8 PPR points, 4.5 short of our 12.3 projection.
